description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): separates the two linked open items — the A >= 5 geometric saturation and 'deriving the octahedral arrangement' — into questions with different answers. DERIVED: (1) every hardcoded deltahedron edge count in gap2_irreducible_triple_bracket_probe IS Euler's E = 3A - 6 for a simplicial polyhedron, so the counts were never a free choice; (2) 3A - 6 = C(A,2) exactly at A = 3 and 4, since A^2 - 7A + 12 = (A-3)(A-4), so the 'A <= 4 simplex, A >= 5 saturates' boundary is a quadratic root; (3) at A = 6 the degree sum forces 4-regularity, and there are 15 labelled but exactly ONE isomorphism class of 4-regular graph on 6 vertices — the octahedron — so the arrangement is forced. NOT DERIVED, and worse than the bean recorded: the LABELLING. 6Li's 20 labellings fall into (8,8,0) x12 and (6,6,0) x8, giving +29.99 % and -2.50 %; the obvious extremal principle (a bound state maximises its binding contacts) selects the +29.99 % class, so the favourable -2.50 % is a pick AGAINST the only principle available, not merely a member-pick. 7Li spans M2 = 7..10 across labellings. All conditional on the convex-deltahedron hypothesis, not derived here, which has no A = 11 member. No fit; no new binding claim.
caveats: Everything in sections 1-3 is conditional on the arrangement being a CONVEX DELTAHEDRON — the corpus's modelling choice, not derived here. Two consequences, cited from the Freudenthal-van der Waerden classification rather than proved: convex deltahedra exist only for A in {4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12}, so there is NO A = 11 member and the model has a hole there that no labelling argument can fill; and maximum-contact packings and convex deltahedra are not the same family in general, so the two terms should not be used interchangeably above A = 9. Within 4 <= A <= 7, where the corpus uses it, they agree.

The a_D values and B(D) anchor are the corpus's own and are used ONLY to reproduce the two figures the bean already publishes (31.193 / -2.50 % and 41.590 / +29.99 %). No fit is performed and no new binding claim is made; the finding is about which labelling an extremal principle selects, not about the value.
